newsitem.title: JAPAN: Glencore to supply bulk of Thai Copper concentrate.
newsitem.headline: Glencore to supply bulk of Thai Copper concentrate.

text.p: Glencore AG will supply "much more than half" of the copper concentrate needs of Thai Copper Industries Public Co's smelter when it begins operations in the autumn of 1998, an Asia-based Glencore official said on Friday.

He declined to give further details on the volume, although trade sources said it was thought to amount to virtually all of the concentrates that will be needed by the smelter, which is scheduled to produce 185,000 tonnes of refined copper per year.
The Glencore official said the contracts covered a period of more than five years but he did not give an exact figure.

Referring to a Thai copper announcement earlier this week that the two sides signed an agent's agreement and a frame contract agreement, he said Glencore, a Swiss-based trade house, was seeking to build up relationships in the region.
"We're not just spot dealers. We value long-term relationships," he said, noting that Glencore owns a stake in Australian copper mining operations.
He added that no contracts had yet been concluded between copper mining companies and the Thai smelter.
He said Glencore already has copper concentrate contracts in the Far East, including smelters in Japan, the Philippines and South Korea, totalling more than 800,000 tonnes per year.
